prospect.name: Anthony
prospect.training_background: Former professional BMX rider; recently restarting BMX and taking tennis lessons; owns one 25 lb kettlebell and follows ad-hoc YouTube workout sessions once or twice a week; dislikes conventional gyms
prospect.medical: History of multiple fractures from BMX ('I broke pretty much all of my bones') which he reports fully healed; states no current injuries, stiffness or movement limitations. Volunteered 'I don't sleep at night' alongside high self-reported energy and heavy coffee intake; not probed further by the rep.

signals: Business owner whose health has been deprioritised for the business, now wants it as a performance input: 'I need to also prioritize my health for the business to keep succeeding'
Explicitly good-to-great framing: 'It's fine, but I wish I was a little bit sharper... I don't want to be huge'
Athletic history and active now (BMX, tennis) rather than deconditioned
Counter-signal: real price resistance — 'I've never spent that much money in anything like that' — which is untypical of the optimizer

goals.text: Lose some weight, particularly belly fat, and get 'a little bit sharper' without adding much size
Build durable training and nutrition habits now that he has turned 30 so he stays in good shape long term
Stay healthy long term so the body can carry the stress of a growing business
Learn correct technique and programming so he can eventually run it himself: 'help me just build a program that I can learn'
Have a full-body system he can do anywhere while travelling, with no bike or tennis court needed
Avoid injuring himself by training with bad form from online videos

pains.text: No consistency with food — swings between eating badly for days and over-correcting; overeats and eats too fast
No structure or knowledge — training off random YouTube sessions and does not feel he is learning anything
Worried he is doing movements wrong and could hurt himself
Dislikes gyms and finds isolated machine work pointless and boring
Business growth brings a lot of stress and has crowded out health for years
Travel and weather break his BMX/tennis routine
Reports not sleeping at night; drinks a lot of coffee (owns coffee shops)

objections.raw_quote: Okay. It's a lot of money
objections.rep_response: Reframed as 'It's an investment in yourself' and moved straight to isolating the money: 'out of the money aspect, right? Do you feel like, yeah, Richard, this is something I want to do?'

objections.raw_quote: I've never spent that much money in anything like that, you know, and it would be a big ask because all of my money is in my business right now, so, you know, I'm being very careful, but I see the value, I get it, you know, but if there's a way to be a bit more reasonable on the, like, payment plans like that, I could consider it
objections.rep_response: Offered an internal six-month plan at $1,200/month, stated it would be 'a little bit more because there's interest', asked for credit score (720) and floated third-party financing. Did not take the full financial picture (cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, investments).

objections.raw_quote: No, not clarification. I just want to review and just give it some thoughts. That's it.
objections.rep_response: Asked what he wanted to look out for, then 'do you feel like it is worth 6k?', then agreed to send a written summary and rebooked for the same time the following week. Did not run the deciding-not-thinking or identity moves.

objections.raw_quote: Maybe I should wait a little. A bit longer because of my finances as well, you know, these different things.
objections.rep_response: Did not address the timing frame at all; moved to asking what he wanted sent over.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Internal plan: $1,200/month for six months (total $7,200), described by the rep as 'a little bit more because there's interest'. Alternative floated: third-party financing, terms unknown and unverified on the call.

evidence: Prospect asked for a written summary before deciding: 'if you can send me an email, like just to summarize everything we talked about, that would be great. And then I can review it and make a decision based on that.'
No payment taken, no link sent, no verbal agreement.
Follow-up call agreed for the same time the following week; rep to send the calendar invite.
Counter-evidence on intent: prospect volunteered 'I see the value, I get it' and 'If I decide to not move forward, I will let you know that also. I won't ghost you.'
Counter-evidence against intent: 'Maybe I should wait a little. A bit longer because of my finances as well.'
outcome.next_step: Rep sends an email summarising the value and the two payment options; follow-up call booked for the same time next week.

notable.note: Prospect explicitly named the sales process while it was running — 'I've been exactly where you are a few years ago. I know the speech, the structure of the speech, the question, and everything... You're making me say out loud the things I want to be' — and the rep did not adapt. Prospect also disclosed 'I don't sleep at night' and heavy coffee consumption; the rep joked about the coffee and moved on rather than treating it as a baseline finding. The payment plan quoted live ($1,200 x 6 = $7,200) exceeds the $6,000 list price.

quality.notes: Frequent inversion of short turns. Clear examples: at 00:02:25 the 'Anthony' block contains the rep's question about strength training while the following 'Richard Claessen' line contains 'I have one, 25 pounds' which is Anthony's. Around 00:09:57 to 00:11:11 a long unbroken block attributed to Richard contains both sides of the exchange. Roles read from content throughout.
